en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on Those Who Were Maidens.
71. The Training Rule on Those Who Were Maidens.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the bhikkhunīs were ordaining girls who were less than twenty years of age.
They were unable to endure cold, heat, hunger, thirst, and the touch of gadflies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and creeping things; they were unable to endure harsh and offensive words;
and they were of a nature unable to endure arisen bodily feelings that were painful, sharp, piercing, bitter, disagreeable, unpleasant, and life-threatening.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... they complained, grumbled, and became indignant, saying:
"How indeed can these bhikkhunīs give the full admission to a maiden less than twenty years of age? ...
[The Buddha asked: "Is it true, monks, that these bhikkhunīs are giving the full admission to maidens less than twenty years of age?"
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How can these bhikkhunīs, monks, give the full admission to a maiden who is less than twenty years old? This is not suitable, monks, for the training of the bhikkhunīs.”
“Monks, a maiden who is less than twenty years of age is unable to endure cold and heat … [and so on] … she is by nature one who cannot tolerate life-threatening conditions.
But a maiden who is exactly twenty years of age, monks, is able to endure cold and heat … [and so on] …”
She is of a nature to endure things that take away life.
Monks, this does not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And so, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule as follows:
“Whichever nun, however, should give the full admission to a maiden who is less than twenty years of age, there is an offense entailing confession (pācittiya).
“Whichever nun” means whichever nun of whatever kind... [and so forth].
"A bhikkhunī" ...
[as before] ... this is the type of bhikkhunī intended in this context.
"Less than twenty years old" means:
"Under twenty years of age.
"A maiden" refers to a female novice (sāmaṇerī).
“Should give the full admission” means:
she should confer the higher ordination (*upasampadā*).

If, thinking “I will give the full admission,” she seeks out a group, a preceptor (*ācariyā*), an alms-bowl, or a robe; or if she demarcates a boundary, there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
For the motion, there is an offense of wrong-doing (*dukkaṭa*).
For the two formal proclamations, there are offenses of wrong-doing.
At the conclusion of the formal proclamation, it is an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) for the preceptor (*upajjhāyā*).
For the community and for the preceptor, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If she gives the full admission to one who is less than twenty years old and perceives her as being less than twenty, there is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
If she gives the full admission to one who is less than twenty years old while being in doubt, there is an offense of wrong-doing.

If she gives the full admission to one who is less than twenty years old, perceiving her to be of full age, there is no offense. If she gives the full admission to one who is of full twenty years of age, perceiving her to be less than twenty, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If she gives the full admission to one who is of full twenty years of age, being in doubt, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If she is twenty years old and she perceives her as such,
there is no offense.
There is no offense if she ordains one who is less than twenty years old while perceiving her as being twenty years old.
If one who perceives her to be twenty years of age gives the full admission to a girl who is actually twenty years of age,
and she is insane,
and she is the first offender— [there is no offense].
The first training rule is concluded.
